newsitem.title: POLAND: Hyundai mulls $1 bln Polish investments.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai mulls $1 bln Polish investments.

text.p: South Korea's Hyundai is considering investing as much as $1.0 billion in Poland in the next several years, Hyundai Corporation Europe GmbH's managing director said.
Young Y. Hwang said Hyundai planned to invest in machinery industry, car industry, construction industry, production of bicycles and others, but gave no details.

"As far as heavy industry is concerned, the scale of our investment would be double digit million dollar figure ... but when we are talking about the whole project it could be at least a billion dollars," he told a news conference.

He told Reuters after the conference that Hyundai would like to form joint ventures with Western companies, already present on the Polish market or willing to enter it, to take advantage of their better knowledge of the market.

The president of Universal, which has set up a joint venture with Hyundai to assemble its Accent cars, also present, said his company was still hoping to get a permit for importing duty-free car parts, required by a recent regulation.
"We hope that after negotiations (with the industry ministry) the problem will be solved positively and we will get the licence," Jerzy Napiorkowski said.
The industry ministry earlier said Universal should not get the licence saying the plant it owns in Pultusk, near Warsaw, does not fulfil requirements of an assembly centre.
